children: Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRK.A) (NYSE:BRK.B), the insurance-and-industrial conglomerate, completed its split succession Friday by naming Howard Buffett chairman and Warren Buffett (Trades, Portfolio) chairman emeritus. Class B shares fell $506.71, extending the market's cautious reaction to a leadership structure that now spreads responsibilities once concentrated around Warren Buffett (Trades, Portfolio).

Greg Abel keeps the operating wheel as CEO, while Howard Buffett takes a nonexecutive chairmanship focused on preserving Berkshire's culture and long-term operating philosophy. Warren Buffett (Trades, Portfolio) remains a director and can still offer advice, but the formal transition is now unmistakable: Berkshire's operating leadership, board stewardship and founder influence sit in separate hands rather than under one legendary capital allocator.

The handoff is happening from a position of strength. Second-quarter operating profit climbed 16% to $12.98 billion, shifting the investor question away from near-term financial pressure and toward whether Berkshire can preserve its decentralized model, disciplined capital allocation and unusually candid shareholder culture across a new generation of leadership. The valuation picture adds another wrinkle: at $506.71, Berkshire trades 8.35% below its GF Value estimate of $552.87, suggesting the shares are priced below GuruFocus' estimate of fair value as investors digest the succession transition.

title: Berkshire Hathaway Falls as Buffett Hands Howard the Chair
